company_items.summary: AutoZone reported FQ4 EPS of $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — 145 basis points of gross margin tailwind came from tariff refunds and 105 basis points from a non-cash LIFO benefit. Domestic comps missed at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and said they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 growth.

Cognex announced an acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80-90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal expands Cognex's exposure to the fast-growing robotics and AI hardware space.

MillerKnoll posted solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and importantly the beat holds even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind — adjusted EPS of 42 cents still topped consensus. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed to $3.88-4.03 billion from $3.93-4.13 billion, while EPS guidance was left unchanged at $1.85-2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1, with interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings extensive experience, having previously served as CFO at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership transition event with no financial results involved.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the Street's 13.85% estimate, as management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation weighing on consumer budgets. Revenue of $2.311 billion came in above the Street's $2.17 billion estimate but still declined 8.4% year-over-year. Some bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction efforts, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in North American towable RV order backlog, though formal fiscal 2027 guidance won't be provided until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares surged in pre-market trading after the company reported positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. This is a significant data readout that validates the drug's competitive positioning in the high-stakes weight loss therapy market. The result is a meaningful catalyst for the stock given intense investor focus on the GLP-1 space.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd, with no broad macro or rates commentary included in today's newsletter. Let's go through the key movers before the open.

Starting with AutoZone — the company beat fiscal fourth quarter earnings at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the quality of that beat is the issue. About 145 basis points of gross margin help came from tariff refunds and another 105 basis points from a non-cash LIFO benefit. Strip those out and the picture is less impressive. Domestic comps came in at just plus 1.6% versus expectations of plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did say sales improved in the final eight weeks of the quarter and they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027. Call it a mixed print — beat on the headline, but execution underneath was soft.

Cognex is making a deal — acquiring RealSense, the depth-sensing camera and robotics perception company, for roughly $500 million upfront plus another $106 million. RealSense is expected to do $80 to $90 million in revenue with more than 50% year-over-year growth. This is a direct bet on the Physical AI and robotics wave and is bullish for Cognex's long-term positioning.

MillerKnoll delivered a solid beat — 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents — and importantly, even backing out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still beat at 42 cents. Sales missed at $923 million versus $943 million expected, but orders were up 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was nudged lower, but EPS guidance held. Mixed, but leaning positive given the earnings quality.

For THOR Industries, it's a miss — 78 cents versus 87 cents expected, with gross margins down 230 basis points year-over-year. Management's tone was cautious, pointing to interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation squeezing consumer budgets. That said, North American towable RV backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year, and dealer inventory is described as healthy. No formal fiscal 2027 guidance yet — that comes later in the fall.

The biggest pre-market mover is Viking Therapeutics — shares are spiking after the company reported 22% weight loss results from its GLP-1 drug VK2735 trial. This is a major positive data readout in one of the most watched therapeutic categories in biotech right now. Clearly bullish.

Pentair named a new CFO, Bob Hau, effective November 1st, bringing in experience from Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Routine leadership transition — not a major catalyst either way.

Bottom line for today: the GLP-1 data from Viking is the headline mover in biotech. AutoZone's quality of beat will be scrutinized. And Cognex's deal puts it squarely in the Physical AI conversation. No broad macro directional call in today's note — it's a stock-picker's morning.
